frequency_question: How often do historical precursors of secondary financial sanctions on major foreign counterparties proceed to full implementation within a comparable multi-year window?
membership_rule: Includes any formal U.S. designation or restriction of a tier-1 foreign commercial entity for facilitating petroleum trade with a heavily sanctioned state; excludes purely domestic or minor intermediary penalties.

cases.name: Sanctions on Bank of Kunlun and EFG-Bank (Iran sanctions related)
CAATSA implementation against designated Russian energy/financial links
Secondary sanctions on Chinese entities over Iranian oil (Zhuhai Zhen Rong)
Sanctions on various small/medium Chinese and non-Chinese entities for Iranian/Russian oil transport

provenance_note: 4 cases named, 6 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (1.5x)
coverage_note: 4 named major instances of systemic extraterritorial enforcement; estimated 6 total comparable historical flashpoint cycles where primary-to-secondary sanction escalation was actively threatened.
known_gaps: Excludes minor or non-public administrative warnings issued to foreign financial institutions that did not result in formal SDN list designations.
skeleton: Major geopolitical confrontation cycles involving systematic evasion of primary energy embargoes by systemic adversary banking networks, partitioned into distinct sanction enforcement waves over three decades.
multiplier: 4 documented major escalation waves with systemic tier-1 target implementation across approximately 6 distinct major sanctions regimes targeting energy trade since 1995.
validity_reason: The geopolitical frameworks governing secondary sanctions and energy embargoes remain structurally consistent across U.S. administrations, though shifting global alliance dynamics could alter baseline enforcement frequencies over a multi-year horizon.
